title: A field actor's model: res/field/actors/<code>/data.json
description: An object code's record of the field actors' model table (archive a/0/4/7, FieldActorConfig in include/field/field_actor.h, with swan's names), which tools/data/field_actor_data.py packs in the order of generated/obj_codes.txt. Its graphics are the directory's sprite.png and sprite.pal, or model.nsbmd, which the packer puts in a/0/4/8 and gives the record the place of.

type.description: The actor's graphics (entityType): none, a sprite of sprite.png's frames, or a 3D model

model.description: For a model, the object code whose model.nsbmd it shows, when it has none of its own

sprite.description: For a sprite, the object code whose sprite.png and sprite.pal it shows, when it has none of its own

sprite_batch.description: For a sprite of its own, the group its graphics come in, 0 if none: a/0/4/8 has the sprites of each batch after those of the batches before it, in code order within one. Paper White 2's followers have it where Pokeweb's installer added their sprites later

texture_set_format.description: For a sprite of its own, how its texture set is written: as the game's (the default), or as Pokeweb's Following Pokémon installer wrote them, with textures named following0 and on, a palette named following, and no search trees

follower.description: Paper White 2: the Following Pokémon this sprite shows, its row of the follower registry and of the positioning table (tools/paperwhite2/following_data.py, docs/paperwhite2/following-pokemon.md). Only the rows after the original's, OBJ_CODE_FOLLOWER_, have one

sex.description: Its sex, null for a species without one

shiny.description: Whether it is the shiny one

placeholder.description: Whether its art stands in for the Pokémon's own (Pokeweb's editor marks these; the runtime ignores it)

animation_profile.description: Whether its right-facing frames mirror the left-facing ones (6 frames) or have their own (8 frames)

art_offset.description: How far its art is from the center: x limits its side gap, y moves it up or down as drawn, z is unused

side_gap.description: The spacing its art needs at its sides, from the art

gaps.description: The walking gap behind the player when the player faces each way, in world units (16 a tile)

shadow.description: Whether the actor casts a shadow (enableShadow)

gender.description: The actor's sex, null for none

collision.description: The tiles the actor takes (collWidth, collHeight)

offset.description: Where it is drawn from its place (wPosOffsetX, Y and Z)
